pdf.why: Go's and Rust's PDFs of the same tree rasterise to the same pixels

pdf/usvg-text-export-cff.why: the CFF subset draws the outlines unhinted, Rust's keeps the font's hints (Windows measured 0.34% beyond 8, mean 0.19)

pdf/usvg-text-export-variable.why: instanced TrueType glyphs: the varied outlines round to integers as write-fonts does, implied points can round differently (Windows measured 0.043% beyond 8, mean 0.006)

png.why: the PDF rasterizer's anti-aliasing, glyph rendering and image smoothing are not resvg's (Windows measured at most 1.18% beyond 32, mean 1.28, outside the entries below)

png.pdftoppm.why: not measured: poppler's Splash anti-aliasing and image smoothing differ from resvg's like Windows' (bound set from the Windows outliers; Linux not run)

png.windows/render-svg-paint.why: Windows.Data.Pdf does not paint function shadings with PostScript functions (repeating and reflecting linear gradients), in Rust's PDF too (measured 24.1%, mean 25.2)

png.windows/render-svg-filters-light.why: the 4x filter raster of high-contrast lighting is downsampled by the PDF renderer (measured 4.3%, mean 4.07)

png.windows/render-svg-filters-misc.why: 4x filter rasters downsampled by the PDF renderer (measured 1.03%, mean 1.58)

png.windows/usvg-filter-functions-drop-s.why: 4x filter raster downsampled by the PDF renderer (measured 1.58%, mean 0.68)

png.windows/render-images-images-gif-web.why: the PDF renderer smooths image samples its own way, resvg uses each image-rendering's filter (measured 7.5%, mean 5.47)

png.windows/render-images-images-jpeg.why: image smoothing as above, and Go's JPEG decode in the PNG (measured 3.46%, mean 3.59)
